meta.title: InfoBIM — Construction information, finally connected
meta.description: InfoBIM connects schedules, documents, photos, and technical data into a traceable view of the project.

hero.title: Your project already produces data. InfoBIM makes that data work together.
hero.lead: Schedules, documents, photos, reports, and technical requirements stop being isolated files and become a traceable operational view of the project.
hero.primaryCta: I want to organize my project

proof1.title: Keep your existing tools
proof1.body: InfoBIM starts with the files your team already uses.

proof2.title: Project-wide traceability
proof2.body: Every piece of information retains its source, context, and relationships.

proof3.title: Humans in command
proof3.body: Automation supports decisions; it does not invent them.

mock.title: Infrastructure workfront
mock.workstreamBody: Scope, drawings, owners, evidence, and decisions gathered in the same context.
mock.activity: Schedule connected to documents and field evidence

problem.eyebrow: The problem is not a lack of information
problem.title: It is too much information, spread too far.
problem.lead: On a real construction site, decisions depend on bringing together what is scattered across schedules, PDFs, emails, photos, spreadsheets, and the team’s memory.

card1.title: Files without context
card1.body: The document exists, but nobody can safely tell which activity, location, version, or decision it belongs to.

card2.title: History trapped in people
card2.body: When someone leaves, changes workfronts, or is simply unavailable, part of the project disappears with them.

card3.title: Decisions without traceability
card3.body: Answering “why was it done this way?” requires archaeology across messages, attachments, and conflicting versions.

case.title: An industrial project. No BIM. And still, connected information.
case.lead: InfoBIM was applied to a finishing-stage project with intense field routines, fragmented documentation, and decisions that had to survive the pace of execution.
case.quote: The value did not come from demanding a perfect model. It came from connecting what the project already produced and making it searchable.

before.label: Before
before.title: Fragmented information
before.item2: Photos with no explicit relationship to activities
before.item3: Drawings, emails, and permits in different sources
before.item4: Technical history dependent on team memory

after.label: With InfoBIM
after.title: Operational context
after.item2: Documents and photos linked to the corresponding work
after.item3: Workfronts organized through 5W2H and verifiable relations
after.item4: Local, navigable dashboard delivered with the project

how.title: An implementation that starts with operational reality.

step1.title: Map
step1.body: We identify sources, routines, owners, and the questions that consume time today.

step2.title: Connect
step2.body: We relate activities, documents, evidence, locations, requirements, and decisions.

step3.title: Deliver
step3.body: The team receives a navigable, traceable view suited to the available environment.

step4.title: Evolve
step4.body: New automations are added as usage proves value — without starting with an endless transformation program.

outcomes.title: Less time searching. More confidence to decide.

card1.title: Find by context
card1.body: Search by activity, workfront, date, document, or relation — not by remembering a file name.

card2.title: Preserve history
card2.body: Source, version, and connections remain with the information that supported the decision.

card3.title: Automate with control
card3.body: Rules and AI operate over structured context; technical decisions remain human.

card4.title: Deliver usable information
card4.body: The project does not end as a dead folder. It ends with a navigable basis for operations and audits.

openSource.title: No black box. No lock-in for project data.
openSource.body: InfoBIM’s core is open source. This enables auditability, adaptation, and continuity without turning engineering information into a platform hostage.

contact.title: Bring the question your team takes too long to answer.
contact.body: We assess the available sources, the current workflow, and a viable scope to demonstrate operational value — without asking the project to stop and “go digital.”
contact.note: Direct channel to the InfoBIM community

footer.tagline: Connected, traceable, and usable engineering information.
footer.note: Developed in Brazil. Built to work where engineering happens.
